codeReview.summary: The workflow implements the requested CI steps and tooling, but the concurrency key does not enforce branch-level cancellation for push events.

issues.description: Concurrency is configured as `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}`. On push events `github.head_ref` is empty, so this falls back to `github.run_id` (unique per run), which prevents cancel-in-progress from cancelling prior runs on the same branch. This violates the requirement to cancel stale runs per branch.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The feature is tagged with `skillName: cli-feature`, but the worker could not use that skill at runtime and had to proceed without it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: features.json sets `github-actions-ci` skillName to `cli-feature`; transcript skeleton shows `Tool: Skill {"skill":"cli-feature"}` followed by 'The `cli-feature` skill isn't available'; handoff.skillFeedback.deviations records the same mismatch.

summary: Fail: one blocking issue found in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` where concurrency grouping uses `github.run_id` fallback, so stale push runs on the same branch are not cancelled as required.
